extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent practitioners preparing and filing U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for securing a filing date and completing U.S. patent applications (nonprovisional, provisional, continuation/divisional/CPA), including what must be filed, timing for missing parts, fees/surcharges, and consequences of non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claim or drawing submitted after the filing date may not contain new matter. Amendments (including submission of claims and drawings) after filing must not introduce subject matter that would have been new matter in the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution application (CPA) confidentiality waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a continued prosecution application will be construed to include a waiver of confidentiality by the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 122 to the extent that any member of the public entitled under § 1.14 to access copies/information concerning either the prior application or any continuing application may be given similar access concerning the other application(s) in the file jacket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a CPA exposes related application information to public access in the same manner as the prior application; applicants should be aware of public availability implications when filing a CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific reference requirement for CPA under 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an application under 37 CFR 1.53(d) is the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 to every application assigned the application number identified in such request. No amendment in an application under this paragraph may delete this specific reference to any prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CPA request itself must include the specific reference and that reference cannot be removed by amendment; retain the reference to preserve the statutory benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to furnish when requesting application under 1.53(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to identifying the prior application's number, the applicant should furnish in the request the following relating to the prior application to the best of his or her ability: (i) Title of invention; (ii) Name of applicant(s); and (iii) Correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplying these items helps the Office process the CPA request and links the CPA correctly to the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and correction of filing date defects
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application deposited under the applicable paragraphs does not meet the requirements to be entitled to a filing date, the applicant will be notified (if a correspondence address is provided) and given a period of time within which to correct the filing error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request for an application under paragraph (d) fails because the filing was not a design application (and if the original application was filed on/after certain dates), the request may be treated as a request for continued examination under § 1.114. Failure to correct within the time provided may result in treatment described in the rules (e.g., termination/abandonment). Specific timelines depend on which requirement is missing and whether a correspondence address was provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for review of filing-date notification; fee and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for review of a notification that the application lacks required papers (or a notification pursuant to paragraph (e)(1)) must be by petition pursuant to this paragraph accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(f). Such petitions must be timely (§ 1.181(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the absence of a timely petition, the filing date of an application in which applicant was notified of a filing error will be the date the filing error is corrected. See fee schedule and timing rules in the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to correct filing errors within time
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is notified of a filing error but fails to correct it within the given period or otherwise timely take action, proceedings in the application will be considered terminated. The application may be disposed of and filing fees (less the handling fee in § 1.21(n)) will be refunded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination for failure to correct is final unless otherwise reversed by timely petition; applicants should act within the notice period to avoid loss of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of nonprovisional application: missing fees, claims, or oath/declaration (correspondence address present)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application accorded a filing date does not include the basic filing fee, search fee, or examination fee, or (for certain filings) at least one claim or the inventor's oath/declaration, and the applicant has provided a correspondence address (§ 1.33(a)), the applicant will be notified and given a period of time within which to supply the missing items to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will send a notice to file missing parts when a correspondence address exists; the applicant must respond within the period set in that notice (timing varies by case) to avoid abandonment. Payment of surcharges required by § 1.16(f) may also be required when filing items later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of nonprovisional application: missing items when no correspondence address provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application has a filing date but lacks required items (basic filing/search/examination fees, at least one claim, or inventor's oath/declaration) and the applicant has not provided a correspondence address, the applicant has three months from the filing date to file claims, pay fees, and pay any required surcharge to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-month deadline applies in absence of a correspondence address; failure to meet the deadline results in abandonment. This rule mirrors the notice-to-file-missing-parts practice when no address was provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and conditions for filing the inventor's oath or declaration (postponement allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor's oath or declaration in an application under § 1.53(b) must be filed within the periods specified, except that filing of the oath/declaration may be postponed until the application is otherwise in condition for allowance under specified conditions: (i) the application must be an original (non-reissue) application that contains an application data sheet identifying each inventor's legal name and mailing/residence address; and (ii) the applicant must file each required oath/declaration in compliance with § 1.63 (or substitute statement under § 1.64) no later than the date the issue fee is paid. This time limit is not extendable under § 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the oath/declaration is postponed, payment of the surcharge under § 1.16(f) is required unless the surcharge was paid on filing or a deposit-account authorization exists. The Office may dispense with the notice to file missing parts if a compliant ADS and other conditions are satisfied. Failure to timely file the oath/declaration (within these constraints) risks abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge and deposit-account treatment when oath/declaration is delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of the surcharge under § 1.16(f) is required if the inventor's oath or declaration is not submitted on filing. If a general authorization to charge required fees to a deposit account is submitted on filing, the Office will charge the surcharge per the deposit-account authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The surcharge cannot be postponed until Notice of Allowance or payment of issue fee; it must be paid within the time specified in § 1.53(f)(1) or (f)(2) unless the Office waives the notice due to a prior compliant ADS and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims, multiple dependent, and application size fees: payment or cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: If excess claims fees required by § 1.16(h) and (i) and the multiple dependent claim fee required by § 1.16(j) are not paid on filing or on later presentation of the claims, those fees must be paid or the claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the time period set for reply by the Office in any notice of fee deficiency. Similarly, if an application size fee under § 1.16(s) is due, it must be paid prior to the expiration of the time period set for reply in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to notices of fee deficiency; unpaid fees can lead to cancellation of claims or abandonment of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office disposition if basic filing fee not paid during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant does not pay the basic filing fee during the pendency of the application, the Office may dispose of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay required filing fees during pendency to avoid disposal; payment is also necessary to permit claiming of benefit in later applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of provisional application: cover sheet and basic filing fee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application must include the cover sheet required by § 1.51(c)(1) (which may be an application data sheet §1.76 or a cover letter identifying the application as provisional) and the basic filing fee (§ 1.16(d)). If a correspondence address is provided, applicant will be notified and given time to file the cover sheet and pay the basic filing fee and any surcharge required by § 1.16(g). If no correspondence address is provided, applicant has two months from the filing date to supply the cover sheet and pay the basic filing fee and surcharge to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include required provisional papers or fees can result in abandonment; if the required figures/drawings are needed for understanding, submit them on filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application conversion to nonprovisional: timing, fees, and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application may be converted to a nonprovisional application and accorded the original filing date of the provisional, but conversion will not entitle applicant to a refund of fees paid in the provisional. A request to convert must be accompanied by the fee in § 1.17(i) and an amendment including at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b), unless the provisional already contains at least one such claim. The resulting nonprovisional must include filing/search/examination fees, the inventor's oath or declaration, and any surcharge required by § 1.16(f) if those items were not present on the provisional filing date. The request must be filed prior to abandonment of the provisional or expiration of 12 months after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion causes the patent term to be measured from at least the provisional filing date; applicants are cautioned that conversion (versus claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e)) may have adverse patent term impacts. No refund or fee credit applies from provisional to nonprovisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional applications are not entitled to certain priorities/benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application is not entitled to the right of priority under 35 U.S.C. 119 or 365(a) or § 1.55, nor to the benefit of an earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) or § 1.78 of any other application. No claim for priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or § 1.78(a)(4) may be made in a design application based on a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not rely on provisional filings to secure priority rights under these statutes; follow the statutory routes for priority/benefit claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules for nonprovisional and design applications (post-Dec 18, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for design applications, for applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after December 18, 2013, the filing date of a nonprovisional application is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received by the Office. For a design application (except a CPA under 1.53(d)), the filing date is the date on which the specification as required by 35 U.S.C. 112, including at least one claim, and any required drawings are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amendments implement PLTIA changes. Although minimal requirements may secure a filing date, applicants are advised that meeting minimal filing-date requirements is not a best practice; include claims and drawings where appropriate to ensure adequate disclosure and avoid loss of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications not forwarded for examination until required parts received (with limited exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under the relevant paragraphs will not be placed on the files for examination until all its required parts, complying with the rules relating thereto, are received; however, the inventor's oath or declaration may be filed when the application is otherwise in condition for allowance and certain minor informalities may be waived subject to subsequent correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, applications may be forwarded for examination even if lacking the inventor's oath/declaration provided a compliant application data sheet is filed. Otherwise, supply required parts promptly to avoid delayed examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.53(d) CPA-specific requirements and filing deadline events
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (a nonprovisional CPA filed on or after December 1, 1997) may be used only for continuation or divisional (not continuation-in-part) of a design application. The prior nonprovisional application must be complete as defined by 37 CFR 1.51(b) (except for the inventor’s oath/declaration in some cases) and contain an ADS indicating name, residence, and mailing address of each inventor. Any application filed under 1.53(d) must disclose and claim only subject matter disclosed in the prior nonprovisional application and must name as inventors the same or fewer inventors than in the prior application. Under 1.53(d), the filing date assigned is the date on which a request, on a separate paper, for an application under 1.53(d) is filed. An application under 1.53(d) must be filed before the earliest of: (A) payment of the issue fee on the prior application (unless a petition under 1.313(c) is granted); (B) abandonment of the prior application; or (C) termination of proceedings on the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs have narrow eligibility (design-only, continuity constraints) and strict timing; ensure subject matter and inventor naming conform to the prior application and that the CPA request is timely filed before the enumerated triggering events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-to-File-Missing-Parts practice and timing for items filed later
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed prior to certain dates, the Office historically issued a Notice to File Missing Parts requiring filing of missing fees or the inventor's oath/declaration within a time period (usually two months) and payment of the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) to avoid abandonment. For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the practice was revised to permit postponement of the oath/declaration until the application is otherwise in condition for allowance under stated conditions, but surcharge payment and timing rules still apply. Payment of surcharge cannot be postponed until Notice of Allowance or issue fee payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the surcharge was not paid on filing, the Office will send a Notice to File Missing Parts requiring it; if a deposit-account authorization was submitted, the Office will charge the surcharge to that account. Monitor notices and respond promptly to avoid abandonment.
